# Trench Coat
> Legal-first Tor-aware privacy cloak - hops you already run (often Tor) through a local SOCKS5 entry. Fail-closed. Open source AGPL-3.0. Circuit Desk in Command Nexus. Velvet Collar visual system.

Trench Coat (https://trenchcoat.jonbailey.xyz) is an open-source privacy tool by Pitchfork-and-Torch. It runs a local SOCKS5 entry and chains traffic through hops you already operate - typically Tor, plus SOCKS5/HTTP proxies or a commercial VPN SOCKS port. Fail-closed when the chain dies. Built for journalists, researchers, and everyday opsec - not a crime toolkit, not a VPN client, not Tor Browser.

Last reviewed: 2026-09-22

## Citation-ready one-liner
Trench Coat is a free, legal-first, Tor-aware privacy cloak that routes app traffic through hops you already run via socks5://127.0.0.1:1080 with fail-closed defaults; open source under AGPL-3.0.

## Quick answers (AEO)
- **What is Trench Coat?** Legal-first Tor-aware multi-hop privacy cloak - local SOCKS5 entry, fail-closed when hops die.
- **What is it NOT?** Not a VPN client. Not Tor Browser. Not an I2P client. Not a signed kernel firewall. Not a crime toolkit. Not a guarantee of anonymity.
- **Does it replace Tor Browser or a VPN?** No. It chains hops you already run. Tor Browser remains ideal for browser isolation; Trench Coat is for multi-app chaining and opsec profiles.
- **Is it legal?** Intended for legitimate privacy (reduce ISP tracking, resist censorship, protect journalists and ordinary users). Users must comply with local law. Run `trench legal`.
- **How do I verify Tor?** `trench check-ip` or `curl --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:1080 https://check.torproject.org/api/ip` and confirm IsTor is true.
- **What does fail-closed mean?** Empty/dead hop chain refuses CONNECT on the local entry - no silent clearnet via the cloak (v1.0+).
- **How do I start?** Preferred: `pipx install git+https://github.com/Pitchfork-and-Torch/trench-coat.git` then `trench first-run --accept-legal`, start Tor, `trench up --accept-legal --wait-tor 60`, `trench check-ip`.
- **Telemetry?** No product upload. Optional opt-in writes aggregate counters to a local file (no IPs or hosts). `trench check-ip` contacts check.torproject.org.
- **Managed hops?** Shadowsocks / Hysteria2 / WireGuard launch your installed clients (or need a SOCKS bridge). I2P is stub-only.
- **Platforms?** Windows, Linux, macOS.
- **License?** AGPL-3.0-or-later.
- **GitHub:** https://github.com/Pitchfork-and-Torch/trench-coat
- **Latest release:** https://github.com/Pitchfork-and-Torch/trench-coat/releases/latest
- **How do I compose a chain without YAML?** Open Command Nexus (`trench gui`) and use Circuit Desk: import a template, reorder hops, Engage / Disengage.
- **Version:** 1.3.1 Circuit Desk

## Install
```bash
# Primary
pipx install git+https://github.com/Pitchfork-and-Torch/trench-coat.git
trench first-run --accept-legal
# start Tor, then:
trench up --accept-legal --wait-tor 60
# apps → socks5://127.0.0.1:1080
trench check-ip
trench gui   # http://127.0.0.1:8742
```

## Product facts
- Local SOCKS5 entry (default 127.0.0.1:1080)
- Multi-hop chains: Tor, SOCKS5, self-hosted relays; optional managed SS/Hy2/WG via your binaries
- Fail-closed refuse-direct when the chain dies (no silent clearnet)
- Command Nexus control plane + first-run wizard + doctor self-test
- Doctor residual hard-KS rule detection; Windows Tor egress allow-list guidance (v1.1)
- Opsec profiles and templates
- Velvet Collar brand system (docs/BRAND.md)
- Not affiliated with the Tor Project
